[MUQATIL:7:7-9/r3] MUQATIL, d. 150 · author | holds | The people with light scales are disbelievers, who lose themselves by denying that the Qur'an came from God.
[IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p165#5/r1] IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB, d. 276 · author | holds | Here yaẓlimūn means they deny God's signs; the root ẓulm has several senses discussed in al-Mushkil.
[TAB-FULL:v10p73/r1] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | Doing wrong to God’s signs means rejecting His proofs and indications instead of affirming their validity and being certain of their truth.
[TAB-FULL:v10p73/r2] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · مجاهد | reports | Mujahid glosses “light scales” as light good deeds.
[TAB-FULL:v10p73/r3] TAB-FULL, d. 310 · author | holds | The singular forms من and فأولئك are used because the sense is plural; using a singular result would also be correct and eloquent.
[IBNABIHATIM:v5p1441/r1] IBNABIHATIM, d. 327 · مجاهد | reports | Mujahid says those whose scales are light are those whose good deeds are few or light.
[IBNABIHATIM:v5p1441/r2] IBNABIHATIM, d. 327 · عبيد الله بن الغيزار | reports | Ubayd Allah ibn al-Ghayzar describes the crowded Resurrection and an angel announcing that the heavy-scaled are blessed forever and the light-scaled are wretched forever.
[THALABI:v4p216/r1] THALABI, d. 427 · author | holds | Weighing deeds tests faith in worldly life, marks the saved and doomed in the next, shows people their recompense, and establishes the proof against them.
[THALABI:v4p216/r2] THALABI, d. 427 · author | holds | The weighing is comparable to the record that speaks with truth and sets out people’s deeds, despite God already knowing them. | mentions 45:29
[THALABI:v4p216/r3] THALABI, d. 427 · مجاهد | reports | Mujahid identifies the heavy balance-pan with a person’s good deeds.
[THALABI:v4p216/r4] THALABI, d. 427 · author | holds | The phrase about wronging God’s signs means that they deny them.
[THALABI:v4p216/r5] THALABI, d. 427 · حذيفة | reports | Gabriel weighs people’s deeds; wrongdoers’ good deeds transfer to victims, or victims’ sins are loaded onto them, leaving them burdened like mountains.
[THALABI:v4p216/r6] THALABI, d. 427 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn Abbas describes a balance with tongue and two pans: a believer’s beautiful deeds outweigh sins and lead to Paradise, while a disbeliever’s ugly deeds are light and fall into Hell.
[THALABI:v4p216/r7] THALABI, d. 427 · author | holds | Since deeds are accidents, the weighed objects are written records containing people’s deeds.
[THALABI:v4p216/r8] THALABI, d. 427 · عبد الله بن عمر | reports | A man’s ninety-nine enormous sin-records are outweighed by a tiny card bearing the testimony that there is no deity but God and Muhammad is His messenger.
[THALABI:v4p216/r9] THALABI, d. 427 · author | holds | The weighing is linked to the promise that just balances will be set up for the Day of Resurrection. | mentions 21:47
[THALABI:v4p217/r1] THALABI, d. 427 · author | holds | The plural mawazin may be a plural form with singular meaning, like plural terms in the cited verse and al-Aʿsha’s poetry.
[THALABI:v4p217/r2] THALABI, d. 427 · الأعشى | reports | Al-Aʿsha’s line uses plural ‘breasts’ and ‘forearms’ while intending one of each.
[THALABI:v4p217/r3] THALABI, d. 427 · author | reports | Other interpretations take the plural as the deeds being weighed, or as one great balance with a balance for each servant.
[THALABI:v4p217/r4] THALABI, d. 427 · author | holds | The plural can refer to the whole balance assembly: its two pans, beam, and tongue, which must come together for weighing.
[THALABI:v4p217/r5] THALABI, d. 427 · author | reports | A moral interpretation calls reason the balance distinguishing truth from falsehood, knowledge the balance distinguishing lawful from unlawful, and sound will the balance distinguishing felicity from misery.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p27/r1] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · مقاتل | reports | Muqatil identifies those with light scales as disbelievers.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p27/r2] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn Abbas says a disbeliever's deeds appear in their ugliest form, weigh little, and lead him to the Fire; a believer whose good deeds are light is rescued by the testimony of God's oneness and Muhammad's messengership.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p27/r3] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · author | reports | A further report says the Prophet produces a fingertip-sized card of the believer's blessings upon him; it outweighs his deeds, and the Prophet identifies it when the believer asks who he is.
[WAHIDI-BASIT:v9p28/r1] WAHIDI-BASIT, d. 468 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn Abbas explains losing oneself as arriving at punishment and wronging God's signs as rejecting what Muhammad brought.
[WAHIDI-WAJIZ:7:9-11/r1] WAHIDI-WAJIZ, d. 468 · author | holds | Those with light scales lose themselves through punishment because they denied what Muhammad brought from God.
[JISHUMI:v4p2499/r3] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | Weighing compares two things to reveal their relative measure, then extends metaphorically to prosody and measured speech; thaqal is opposite lightness.
[JISHUMI:v4p2499/r4] JISHUMI, d. 494 · أبو هاشم | reports | Abū Hāshim treats heaviness as a distinct attribute in a heavy object: a necessary downward tendency.
[JISHUMI:v4p2499/r5] JISHUMI, d. 494 · أبو علي | reports | Abū ʿAlī says heaviness reduces to the parts composing the heavy object; they agree that lightness is no positive attribute but the absence of heaviness.
[JISHUMI:v4p2499/r6] JISHUMI, d. 494 · author | holds | Loss means losing one's capital.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p215/r1] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · author | holds | Light scales describe those who deny God’s signs.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p215/r2] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · أبو بكر | reports | Abu Bakr says scales grow heavy through following truth in worldly life, even when truth weighs upon people; following falsehood makes them light.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p215/r3] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · author | reports | One explanation takes the plural form موازين as singular in meaning, like the plural address يا أيها الرسل.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p215/r4] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · author | reports | Another explanation assigns every servant an individual balance.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p215/r5] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · author | reports | A third view posits one great balance with a separate balance suspended for each servant.
[BAGHAWI-FULL:v3p215/r6] BAGHAWI-FULL, d. 516 · author | reports | The plural may also refer to the balance’s two pans and indicator, whose combined parts are needed for weighing.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p375/r2] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · فرقة | reports | One group takes scales and weighing as a metaphor for the meticulous justice of Judgment, using the familiar image of a balance; Abu Talib's verse illustrates this sense.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p375/r3] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | rejects | Ibn Atiyya says the metaphorical view is weaker: Qur'anic wording and a Prophetic report direct a person to seek the Prophet at the visible balance, weighing poses no problem, and abandoning the literal sense without cause risks denying revealed realities.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p375/r4] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · مجاهد، الضحاك | reports | This metaphorical view is also reported from Mujahid, al-Dahhak, and others, who understand heaviness and lightness as the abundance or scarcity of good deeds.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p375/r5] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · جمهور الأمة | reports | The majority say the Judgment balance has a beam and two pans like worldly balances, displaying exact justice through a familiar object.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p375/r6] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · حذيفة بن اليمان | reports | Hudhayfa says Gabriel is the custodian of the balances on Judgment Day.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p376/r1] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | The balance should be understood literally; reports say records of good and bad deeds go into its pans, where God creates heaviness or lightness.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p376/r2] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | Weight must occur in a body, since an accident cannot inhere in another accident; it may occur in the records or nearby bodies, and Abu al-Maali favors the records.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p376/r3] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | Unreliable reports about the balance's shape and length need not be repeated; Hasan's report that each person has a separate balance is rejected because the balance is one, though each person has an individual weighing.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p376/r6] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | God's weighing, recording deeds, and making limbs testify despite His knowledge serve to establish proof; the testimony of divine oneness must tip a person's balance.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p376/r7] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | reports | The author asks how sinful believers can have a weighty balance and be judged successful yet still enter Hell.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p377/r1] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | A light balance means the pan of good deeds rises; they lose themselves through destruction and eternal residence in Hell.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p377/r2] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | Bi-mā expresses recompense, like thanking someone for what they did; mā is a verbal noun, and God's signs are proofs, commands, and prohibitions that they wrong by disbelief and denial.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p377/r3] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · طائفة | reports | One answer is that good deeds are weighed without tawhid first, then tawhid makes the balance heavy when sinful believers are released from Hell.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p377/r4] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | Knowing that a sinner will not remain forever in Hell counts as success, even if disciplinary punishment comes first.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p377/r5] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · طائفة | reports | One answer is that good deeds are weighed without tawhid first, then tawhid makes the balance heavy when sinful believers are released from Hell.
[IBNATIYYA-FULL:v2p377/r6] IBNATIYYA-FULL, d. 542 · author | holds | Knowing that a sinner will n

ot remain forever in Hell counts as success, even if disciplinary punishment comes first.
[TABRISI:7:8-9/r4] TABRISI, d. 548 · author | holds | Those with light scales lose themselves by incurring everlasting punishment; their loss is the destruction of their greatest capital, the self, through wrongdoing and denial of Muhammad's signs.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p169#2/r1] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · author | holds | God will report to the messengers and nations what they did, knowing it and never being absent from them.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p169#2/r2] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · ابن عباس | reports | The record will be placed and will speak of what people used to do.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p169#4/r1] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · author | reports | Yazlimun means either deny or disbelieve.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p169#4/r2] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · الفراء | reports | Mawazin means weight; Arabic uses “your scale” or “your house's scale” to mean equal to or beside it, as a poem uses mizan for a person's words.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p169#4/r3] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · author | holds | Belief in the scale is well established in hadith and is the Qur'an's plain sense, though the Mu'tazila deny it because deeds are accidents.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p169#4/r4] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص عن النبي | reports | A hadith says a man with ninety-nine vast records receives a card bearing the two testimonies; the card outweighs all records. Ahmad and al-Tirmidhi transmit it.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p169#4/r5] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · أبو هريرة عن النبي | reports | A tall, gluttonous man will weigh no more than a mosquito's wing.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p169#4/r6] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · ابن عباس | reports | Good and bad deeds are weighed on a scale with a tongue and two pans; a believer's good deeds appear beautiful and outweigh the bad, while an unbeliever's appear ugly and are light.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p169#4/r7] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · الحسن | reports | The scale has a tongue and two pans.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p169#4/r8] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · author | reports | In a report, David asks to see the scale and how anyone can fill its pans; God says a date fills them when He is pleased with His servant.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p169#4/r9] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · حذيفة | reports | Gabriel operates the scale; he returns a wronged person's due from the oppressor's good deeds, or transfers the victim's sins to the oppressor if no good remains.
[IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p171/r1] IBNJAWZI-ZAD, d. 597 · author | holds | Although God knows the measure of deeds, weighing them tests belief in this life, displays each person's fate, teaches what good and evil they did, establishes proof, and shows that God is just; recording deeds similarly does not imply fear of forgetting.
[RAZI-FULL:v14p21#2/r1] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | The weighing follows the questioning and accounting described earlier; the phrase can be parsed with يومئذ as an adverb and الحق as predicate, or as predicate with الحق describing a just weighing.
[RAZI-FULL:v14p21#2/r2] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · ابن عباس | reports | One literal view says God sets up a balance with a pointer and two pans; Ibn Abbas says the believer's deeds appear in their best form and good deeds outweigh evil, as in 21:47. | mentions 21:47
[RAZI-FULL:v14p21#2/r3] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · ابن عباس | reports | Ibn Abbas says a believer's deeds are transformed into a beautiful image for weighing, while most exegetes instead say the weighed items are the written records; a prophetic answer to what is weighed is reported as the records.
[RAZI-FULL:v14p21#2/r4] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · عبد الله بن سلام | reports | Ibn Salam describes a balance between jinn and humans facing the Throne, with one pan toward Paradise and one toward Hell, large enough to hold the heavens and earth, watched by Gabriel.
[RAZI-FULL:v14p21#2/r5] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · عبد الله بن عمر | reports | Ibn Umar reports a man whose 99 scrolls of sins, each as long as sight, are outweighed by a tiny card bearing the testimony that none is god but God and Muhammad is His messenger.
[RAZI-FULL:v14p21#2/r6] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · الحسن | reports | Hasan reports that when Aisha asked about people remembering one another at resurrection, the Prophet said they would be barefoot and unclothed and too occupied with records and weighing to remember anyone, citing 80:37. | mentions 80:37
[RAZI-FULL:v14p21#2/r7] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · عبيد بن عمير | reports | Ubayd ibn Umayr says a huge, voracious drinker may have no weight even equal to a gnat.
[RAZI-FULL:v14p22/r1] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · مجاهد والضحاك والأعمش | reports | Mujahid, al-Dahhak, and al-A'mash, followed by many later scholars, take the balance as justice and judgment rather than a literal scale.
[RAZI-FULL:v14p22/r2] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | reports | Supporters of the figurative reading say weight can mean justice because worldly fairness in taking and giving is shown by weights; Arabic also uses weight figuratively for worth and equality, as in 18:105. | mentions 18:105
[RAZI-FULL:v14p22/r3] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | A poem cited by the author uses ميزانه for the balance of an opponent's argument: the speaker had a measure for every disputant, meaning a reply of equal force, not a physical scale.
[RAZI-FULL:v14p22/r4] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | rejects | Razi insists the verse must mean only justice: deeds are transient accidents, so cannot be weighed; even if they persisted, weighing is useless because believers already know God's justice and others could suspect a staged result.
[RAZI-FULL:v14p22/r5] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · أصحاب القول الأول | reports | Literal-scale proponents answer that everyone knows God is just and the scale publicly displays the result: a favorable balance increases joy, an unfavorable one increases grief and shame; some describe light or darkness, others a tilted pan.
[RAZI-FULL:v14p23/r1] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | prefers | Razi finds several actual balances more apparent than one, citing 21:47 and the verse's plural; separate balances may measure heart, bodily, and spoken acts. | mentions 21:47
[RAZI-FULL:v14p23/r2] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · الزجاج | reports | Al-Zajjaj explains the plural either as Arabic using a plural for one object or as referring to the things weighed, meaning deeds rather than balances; Razi says both abandon the plain plural despite no obstacle to multiple scales.
[RAZI-FULL:v14p23/r3] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · author | holds | The heavy and light balances divide humanity into two groups: those whose good deeds exceed their bad and those whose bad exceed their good; no group has equal totals.
[RAZI-FULL:v14p23/r4] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · أكثر المفسرين | reports | Most exegetes identify those whose balances are light as unbelievers, because being described as wronging God's signs means denying them.
[RAZI-FULL:v14p23/r5] RAZI-FULL, d. 606 · الواحدي | reports | Al-Wahidi's al-Basit reports that the Prophet's prayer-card can outweigh a believer's weak good deeds; the wider scholarly report instead gives the card bearing the testimony of faith, which al-Qadi says must be paired with its obligations to avoid encouraging sin.
[BAYDAWI-FULL:7:9/r1] BAYDAWI-FULL, d. 685 · author | holds | Those whose scales are light have lost themselves by wasting their sound original disposition and committing acts that expose them to punishment; they wrong the signs by rejecting them.
[NASAFI-FULL:v2p4#4/r1] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | The light balances belong to unbelievers: lacking faith, they have no good works that count in the scale.
[NASAFI-FULL:v2p4#4/r2] NASAFI-FULL, d. 710 · author | holds | They lose themselves by wronging God's signs; the signs are proofs, and wronging them means denying them and refusing to follow them.
[QASHANI:7:8-9/r1] QASHANI, d. 736 · author | holds | Weighing is assessment of deeds at the lesser resurrection and is just or real; lasting good deeds weigh heavily and yield the heart's paradise of divine attributes.
[QASHANI:7:8-9/r2] QASHANI, d. 736 · author | holds | The scale's tongue is justice, with sense and intellect as its pans; enduring rational acquisitions, virtues, good works, and sincere intentions have weight, unlike transient sensations, desires, and vices.
[QASHANI:7:8-9/r3] QASHANI, d. 736 · author | holds | The light-weight lose themselves by trading original capacity for worldly debris and personal aims, displaying ego qualities and concealing God's qualities in denial of His signs.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p13/r10] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · الحسن | reports | Hasan holds that every person has a separate balance on the Day of Resurrection.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p13/r11] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | reports | Balances can also stand for good deeds by ellipsis: the balance-pan of a person’s weighed deeds becomes heavy or light.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p13/r14] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | The prepositional phrase about God’s signs attaches to wronging because the verb includes the sense of denying or rejecting, and rejection takes bi-.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p13/r15] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | reports | The apparent division includes obedient and sinful believers as well as unbelievers, so unbelievers’ deeds are weighed.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p13/r16] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · قوم | reports | Others say unbelievers receive no balance and are not judged, citing the verse that their deeds become scattered dust; on this view only believers’ deeds are weighed. | mentions 25:23
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p13/r4] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | reports | Exegetes disagree whether the weighing is a real balance or a figure for complete justice, sound judgment, and exact reckoning.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p13/r5] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · المعتزلة | reports | The Muʿtazila, preceded in this view by Mujahid, al-Dahhak, and al-Aʿmash, deny a literal balance and take heaviness and lightness as abundance or scarcity of good deeds.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p13/r6] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · جمهور الأمة | reports | The majority affirm a re

al balance with a shaft, two pans, and a tongue, shown to all creatures to establish proof, justice, and the end of excuses.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p13/r7] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | The visible balance confirms the judgment alongside questioning, people’s admissions, testimony by limbs, prophets, angels, and witnesses.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p13/r8] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · author | holds | Reports say the weighed objects are the records on which deeds were written; God creates heaviness or lightness in them, while reports about the balance’s dimensions and form have unsound chains.
[ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p13/r9] ABUHAYYAN-FULL, d. 745 · جمهور الأمة | reports | The majority explain plural balances by the multiplicity of objects weighed, although there is one balance.
[SAMIN-DURR:7:9/r1] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | holds | بما كانوا modifies خسروا, with ما as a verbal noun; بآياتنا modifies يظلمون and is fronted for the verse ending.
[SAMIN-DURR:7:9/r2] SAMIN-DURR, d. 756 · author | reports | The ba in يظلمون reflects an implied meaning of denial or rejection, comparable to آل عمران 3:11 and النمل 27:14. | mentions 3:11, 27:14
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p389#2/r1] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · ابن عباس | reports | One view weighs deeds themselves, which God turns into bodies; al-Baghawi reports this from Ibn Abbas, with traditions portraying Qur’an, surahs, and righteous deeds as visible forms.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p389#2/r2] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | reports | A second view weighs the record of deeds; the report of the card bearing There is no god but God outweighing ninety-nine scrolls is graded sound by al-Tirmidhi.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p389#2/r3] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | reports | A third view weighs the person: a very heavy man may weigh less than a gnat’s wing, while Ibn Masud’s thin legs outweigh Mount Uhud. | mentions 18:105
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p389#2/r4] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | prefers | Ibn Kathir sees no conflict: deeds, their records or forms, and the people who performed them may all be weighed at different times.
[IBNKATHIR-FULL:v3p389/r1] IBNKATHIR-FULL, d. 774 · author | holds | The scales on Judgment Day weigh deeds with perfect justice; God wrongs no one, and the heavier scale brings success while the lighter one brings ruin. | mentions 21:47, 4:40, 101:6, 101:7, 101:8, 101:9, 101:10, 101:11, 23:101, 23:102, 23:103
[BIQAI-FULL:v3p9/r10] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · author | holds | Those whose scales are light lose their own selves, their chief capital, through persistently putting God's signs in the wrong place.
[BIQAI-FULL:v3p9/r9] BIQAI-FULL, d. 885 · الحسن | reports | Al-Hasan says the scale holding good deeds should naturally grow heavy, while the scale holding sins should grow light.
[DURR-FULL:v3p417/r1] DURR-FULL, d. 911 · رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم | reports | In a dialogue, the Prophet defines faith as belief in God, angels, books, messengers, Paradise and Hell, the balance, resurrection, and divine decree.
[DURR-FULL:v3p417/r10] DURR-FULL, d. 911 · ابن عباس | reports | The balance has a tongue and two pans; heavy scales bring success, while light scales mean losing oneself and one's home in Paradise for wronging God's signs.
[DURR-FULL:v3p417/r2] DURR-FULL, d. 911 · مجاهد | reports | The weighing is justice; heavy scales mean good deeds, and the transmitted gloss for light scales also says good deeds.
[DURR-FULL:v3p417/r3] DURR-FULL, d. 911 · عبد الله بن العيزار | reports | A caller beside the balance announces each person's lasting felicity or misery according to whether the scales are heavy or light.
[DURR-FULL:v3p417/r5] DURR-FULL, d. 911 · وهب بن منبه | reports | Only the endings of deeds are weighed: God grants a good ending to the one He wills good for and an evil ending to the one He wills evil for.
[DURR-FULL:v3p417/r6] DURR-FULL, d. 911 · الحارث الأعور | reports | Truth feels heavy to people of truth as it is heavy on the balance, and light to people of falsehood as it is light there.
[DURR-FULL:v3p417/r9] DURR-FULL, d. 911 · حذيفة | reports | Gabriel oversees the balances: an oppressor's good deeds are transferred to the victim, or the victim's sins to the oppressor if the oppressor has no good deeds.
